beats.title: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang Revolt
beats.description: Conscripts delayed by floods and facing execution rose against the harsh first imperial dynasty of China, sparking mass revolt.

beats.title: Sicily's First Slave War Begins
beats.description: Enslaved workers on Sicilian estates, led by a Syrian named Eunus, seized cities and defied Rome for years.

beats.title: Spartacus Leads the Slave Revolt
beats.description: Gladiators escaped a training school near Capua and built an army of runaway slaves that defeated several Roman legions.

beats.title: Boudica's Revolt
beats.description: A widowed Iceni queen rallied British tribes and burned Roman Colchester, London and St Albans before being crushed.

beats.title: The Great Jewish Revolt
beats.description: Judean rebels drove out the Roman garrison in Jerusalem, starting a rebellion that ended with the Temple destroyed.

beats.title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
beats.description: Followers of a Daoist healer, wearing yellow headcloths, rose by the hundreds of thousands against a failing Han court.

beats.title: Nika Riots in Constantinople
beats.description: Chariot-race factions united against the emperor and burned much of the capital before troops slaughtered the crowd.
beats.why_in: mass urban uprising against the emperor

beats.title: Zanj Rebellion Begins
beats.description: Enslaved East Africans draining salt marshes in Iraq rose against the caliphate and held out for well over a decade.

beats.title: Huang Chao's Rebellion
beats.description: A failed exam candidate turned salt smuggler led starving peasants across China and eventually sacked the capital.
beats.note: Searched: Wikipedia gives 874-884; some sources say 875

beats.title: Flemish Peasant Revolt
beats.description: Farmers and townsfolk in coastal Flanders rebelled against heavy taxes and their count, ruling the countryside for years.

beats.title: The Jacquerie
beats.description: Hungry French peasants attacked castles and nobles in the countryside north of Paris before being brutally put down.

beats.title: Wat Tyler's Peasants' Revolt
beats.description: Marching on London over a poll tax, English commoners burned palaces and confronted the teenage king face to face.

beats.title: Jack Cade's Rebellion
beats.description: Kentish commoners marched on London, killed a royal treasurer and demanded an end to corrupt advisers around the king.

beats.title: Dozsa's Peasant Revolt
beats.description: A crusade army of Hungarian peasants turned on their landlords, and its leader was put to death on a red-hot iron throne.

beats.title: German Peasants' War
beats.description: Farmers across southern German lands, inspired by the Reformation, issued Twelve Articles and rose against their lords.

beats.title: Pilgrimage of Grace
beats.description: Tens of thousands in northern England rose in protest at the closing of monasteries and the policies of Henry VIII.

beats.title: Shimabara Rebellion
beats.description: Overtaxed peasants, many of them persecuted Christians, held a coastal castle in Japan against a shogunate army.

beats.title: Masaniello's Revolt in Naples
beats.description: A young fisherman led the poor of Naples against a tax on fruit and the Spanish viceroy who imposed it.

beats.title: Stenka Razin's Rebellion
beats.description: A Cossack leader gathered peasants and runaways along the Volga in a huge revolt against the tsar's nobles.

beats.title: Pueblo Revolt
beats.description: Pueblo peoples of the Southwest united to drive Spanish settlers and missionaries from their homeland for a dozen years.

beats.title: Pugachev's Rebellion
beats.description: A Cossack claiming to be the murdered tsar raised serfs and Cossacks and threatened Catherine the Great's throne.

beats.title: Tupac Amaru II Rebellion
beats.description: A descendant of Inca royalty led Andean Indigenous and mixed-race people against Spanish taxes and forced labour.

beats.title: Shays' Rebellion
beats.description: Indebted Massachusetts farmers closed courts and marched on an armory, alarming leaders of the young republic.

beats.title: Storming of the Bastille
beats.description: A Parisian crowd seized the royal fortress and prison for its gunpowder, becoming the symbol of a revolution.

beats.title: Irish Rebellion
beats.description: United Irishmen and rural Catholics and Protestants rose against British rule, with fighting from Wexford to Antrim.

beats.title: Swing Riots
beats.description: English farm labourers smashed threshing machines and burned ricks to protest low wages and lost work.

beats.title: Nat Turner's Rebellion
beats.description: An enslaved preacher in Virginia led an overnight uprising against slaveholders that shook the American South.

beats.title: Silesian Weavers' Uprising
beats.description: Starving cloth workers in Prussia destroyed factory owners' houses and machines before soldiers opened fire.

beats.title: Barricades Topple a King in Paris
beats.description: Barricades in Paris toppled a king and set off a wave of uprisings that spread across Europe within weeks.

beats.title: Taiping Rebellion Begins
beats.description: A failed scholar who believed himself Christ's brother led a vast peasant army against China's Qing rulers.

beats.title: Morant Bay Rebellion
beats.description: Poor Black Jamaicans marched on a courthouse over land and justice, and the governor's reprisals shocked Britain.

beats.title: The Paris Commune
beats.description: Working-class Parisians took over their city and ran it as a radical government until troops retook it in a bloody week.
beats.why_in: popular uprising named in the boundary

beats.title: Boxer Rebellion
beats.description: A peasant movement in northern China attacked foreigners and Christians and besieged the embassy quarter in Beijing.

beats.title: Bloody Sunday Sparks Revolution
beats.description: Troops fired on workers petitioning the tsar, setting off strikes and mutinies across the Russian Empire.

beats.title: Bread Riots Topple the Tsar
beats.description: Strikes and bread riots in Petrograd, joined by soldiers, forced the last tsar of Russia to give up his throne.

beats.title: Kronstadt Rebellion
beats.description: Sailors and workers at a naval base near Petrograd rose against the new Bolshevik government and were crushed.

beats.title: East German Workers' Uprising
beats.description: Building workers' strikes in East Berlin grew into nationwide protests until Soviet tanks restored order.

beats.title: Hungarian Uprising
beats.description: Students and workers in Budapest toppled a Stalin statue and fought Soviet forces before the revolt was crushed.

beats.title: Soweto Uprising
beats.description: Black schoolchildren in South Africa marched against being taught in Afrikaans, and police fire turned it into a revolt.

beats.title: Zapatista Uprising
beats.description: Masked Indigenous rebels seized towns in Chiapas on the day a major trade pact took effect, demanding land and rights.

beats.title: Egyptians Occupy Tahrir Square
beats.description: Mass crowds in Cairo, inspired by Tunisia, forced out a president who had ruled for three decades.
